Kimberly —

Heads up: our vendor monitoring flagged a configuration error that may have exposed transaction metadata for a small subset of HearthBank customers. We don't yet have confirmation of egress, but legal/compliance asked us to start the notification cadence. Can you confirm Redwood's contractual obligations for:

- Initial notification timing (we need a written statement that an internal review is underway)
- Scope determination window (how long until you can tell us affected customers / regions)
- Evidence/forensic handover (format, hashes, and secure transfer channel)
- Whether subprocessors keep persistent backups across regions (we're particularly concerned about copies outside the EU)

I've attached our preliminary report — it’s high level. Please let me know the best point of contact on your side and the expected timeboxes so we can brief our internal stakeholders.

Thanks,
Maria Santos

Maria — thanks for the quick flag and for the initial report. We're treating this as a high-priority notification. Tactical next steps from Redwood:

1) Acknowledgement: you have our written acknowledgement now. We'll stand up a joint channel (secure portal + designated case mailbox) for all artifacts.

2) Timeboxes (provisional, subject to evidence):
   - Initial factual acknowledgment: within 24 hours (you have that now).
   - Preliminary scope estimate (affected customer count / regions): within 72 hours.
   - Forensic package ready for secure handover: within 5 business days after scope confirmation.

3) Subprocessor info: we will produce a current subprocessor roster and indicate whether those subprocessors maintain cross-border backups. If there are any regional export restrictions, we will flag them.

4) Evidence transfer: we will push artifacts to Redwood's secure evidence portal (one-time read-only bundle, checksummed). We'll provide SHA256 hashes and a manifest. If HearthBank prefers a mutually agreed transfer method (SFTP/PRIVShare), we can accommodate.

Action items for you: confirm whether the HearthBank compliance team needs a formal written notification under the DPA right now (we can issue the formal notice within the 24-hour window), and if you'd like Redwood to begin lock-and-collect on specific buckets.

Looping in Marissa for contractual language and Karthik for the technical forensics plan.

Best,

Maria / Kimberly —

From a DPA & notification perspective, proposed commitments we can put in writing now (we'll issue a formal notice once HearthBank confirms):

- Initial written notice: within 24 hours of Redwood becoming aware (we have acknowledged).
- Preliminary scope statement: within 72 hours, with best-effort customer counts and affected regions.
- Full evidentiary package: within 5 business days of scope confirmation. If collection requires third-party forensic partners, timelines may extend; we'll notify you immediately.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor list within 24 hours and will flag any subprocessors that store backups outside the EU/UK.
- Cooperation: Redwood will provide reasonable assistance for regulator inquiries and will not unreasonably withhold forensic artifacts; we will, however, redact unrelated customer content where necessary and document any legal restrictions to transfer.

Please note a few legal caveats in the redline (attached): we propose a fixed timebox for preliminary scope but reserve the right to extend the forensic handover if the collection materially requires additional time (e.g., cross-border export approvals or court orders). We can discuss specific language for "reasonable" vs "commercially reasonable" cooperation if HearthBank requires tighter enforceable SLAs.

If HearthBank would like, I can route a signed notice template via DocuSign once we lock the timeboxes — that often helps procurement trigger internal workflows.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference

Maria — technical notes and what we will provide:

- Forensics scope: we'll collect access logs, object access manifests, relevant app logs, and optional memory snapshots if needed. Expect a manifest file with SHA256 hashes for all artifacts.
- Subprocessors called out: EdgeServe Ltd (edgeops.io) — edge caches/backups; ArchiveCloud Inc (archive.cloud) — long-term backups (both maintain cross-region replicas). We'll include their contact points.
- Transfer method: Redwood will publish a one-time read-only bundle to the secure portal (link: https://redwood.secureshare.example.com/portal/exp-HEARTH-20261116) and provide signed hashes. If HearthBank requires export controls paperwork for cross-border movement, let us know and we'll begin the approval flow.
- Minimization: we'll attempt to pseudonymize PII in artifacts where possible, but we may need to deliver raw logs under a narrow legal footing.

Immediate ask from Redwood: confirm the portal access list (names + org emails) for HearthBank so we can provision read-only access and time-limited tokens. Also confirm whether you want continuous streaming access for the next 72 hours or a one-time bundle.

I'll stand up a parallel forensic channel with our third-party incident responder if we need deeper collection.

Karthik Iyer
